headline: The ozone layer shields life from harmful radiation—thin protection with enormous impact
universal_truth: Small shields can block large threats; protection often happens quietly, out of sight
fun_facts: If compressed to sea level pressure, the ozone layer would be only 3 millimeters thick
The ozone hole is healing—the Montreal Protocol is one of humanity's greatest environmental successes
Ozone at ground level is pollution; in the stratosphere, it's protection—context determines function
discussion_questions: What thin protections shield you from large threats?
What would you lose if an invisible shield disappeared?
How do you protect yourself from invisible threats?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: High above you, a molecular sunscreen blocks ultraviolet radiation that would otherwise damage DNA, cause cancer, and harm ecosystems. The ozone layer is just millimeters thick when compressed, yet it protects all life on Earth.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: When we discovered the ozone hole, we acted—and it's now healing. This shows that understanding threats enables protection. What makes protective systems work?

options.text: Effective protection matches the threat—understanding what you're protecting against lets you design appropriate shields, even thin ones that block large dangers
options.response: Yes. Protection doesn't need to be massive—it needs to match the threat. A thin ozone layer blocks specific wavelengths. Understanding threat and mechanism enables efficient protection.

options.text: Bigger, stronger protection is always better
options.response: Sometimes, but targeted protection often beats brute force...

q1.title: Targeted Protection
q1.script: Ozone doesn't block everything—just harmful UV wavelengths. It lets visible light through. Effective protection is specific: blocking what hurts while permitting what helps. Discrimination is key.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Targeted Protection"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Fragile but Fixable
q2.script: We nearly destroyed the ozone layer with CFCs before we understood the threat. But when we learned, we acted—banning the chemicals. The ozone hole is healing. Problems understood can be solved.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Personal Shields
q3.script: You have shields too—boundaries, habits, relationships that protect you from harm. Like ozone, they may be thin and invisible but critical. Identify what protects you and maintain it.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Small shields can block large threats. Protection often happens quietly, out of sight. Know what protects you—and protect it.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 240! Tomorrow, we continue exploring Earth's systems. Until then, identify one thin protection that makes your life possible.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Shield Audit - What Protects You?
growTrack.learning_objective: Identify and maintain personal protective systems
growTrack.activity: What thin but essential protections do you have? Boundaries, habits, relationships, safeguards? Often our most important protections are invisible until they fail. Identify one and consider if it needs maintenance or strengthening.
